arms.predicted: With only 4 heuristics but same SA improvements (cooling, restarts, rotation mode), score will be lower than h-main, demonstrating expanded heuristic space is necessary.
arms.observed: 5 valid runs (excluding 2 server-timing outliers at 89.21, 89.42, 89.45): 95.80, 95.80, 95.81, 95.80, 95.81. Mean = 95.80, std = 0.005. Lower than h-main (96.52) by 0.72 points but higher than iter-2 baseline (95.21) by 0.59 points.
arms.diagnostic_note: h-control-negative (4 heuristics + SA tuning) beats iter-2 (95.21) by 0.59 points, confirming SA improvements (cooling, restarts, rotation mode) contribute independently. h-main (8 heuristics) adds another 0.72 points, confirming expanded heuristics are the larger contributor (0.72 vs 0.59). discrepancy_analysis: Both predictions confirmed. The total gain from iter-2 to h-main is 1.31 points, decomposed as: SA tuning contributes ~0.59 points (h-control-negative vs iter-2), expanded heuristics contribute ~0.72 points (h-main vs h-control-negative). The expanded heuristic space is the larger contributor as predicted, though SA tuning alone accounts for 45% of the improvement — slightly more than expected. Server-timing outliers affect both arms (2/7 h-main runs, 3/8 h-control-negative runs), suggesting ~25-35% of runs hit server load issues.
